items.title: Reliable attached-client baseline
acceptance: Run pinned tmux and freshly built zz with isolated homes/config roots and short sockets; record binary hashes, source revision and dirty state, OS, TERM, shell and dimensions.

Retain attach, input, daemon and outer-screen diagnostics on every geometry-fixture timeout, proven by a driven failure. The geometry-report timeout recorded on macOS on 2026-09-09 is handed to TUI-013 for reproduction or explanation there (clause split 2026-09-09 by fabrico's deferral; reversible).

Produce a repeatable baseline at 80x24, 100x24 and 120x24 with all measured differences and fixture limitations retained, including the waived wide-terminal columns. This package proves fixture reliability, not runtime parity.
items.evidence_note: MEASURED 2026-09-09 on alienware (CachyOS, 16 cores, Linux) from worktree /home/demfabris/dev/zz-tui-lane at 576b6b745821856d9c00b3a62d6a1982fd8571e1, clean apart from this attempt's own files. zz built fresh in that worktree; pinned tmux d77c9dc6, sha256 df2cafcb212e8b69677dd57c2bd0c3bb59592eaf385d974ec0124526d6b63ee5, tmux -V next-3.8. TERM=xterm-ghostty, bash 5.3.15, LANG=en_US.UTF-8 with LC_TIME=pt_BR.UTF-8. environment.txt records both binaries' sha256, the worktree revision and dirty state, the OS, TERM, shell, locale and the sizes each fixture drives. The zz hash identifies the artifact but does not attest it: a cargo debug build of zz is not bit-reproducible on this box, and the cycle-18 reviewer rebuilt -p zz at this same worktree path from the same source and got a different hash, and a third from another worktree. Provenance rests on reproduction instead, which is stronger: that independently built zz reproduced these fixture results and TUI-002's 195 capture files byte for byte. The pin's hash verifies exactly. GEOMETRY: compat/tui-pane-geometry.sh exits 0 SIX times out of six, 4 to 5 seconds a run against its own 10 second bound - three runs of the fixture as it stands at origin/main and three of the fixture after this attempt's timeout-diagnostics change. 80x24 both 80 columns, 100x24 both 100, rows 23 on both sides at all three sizes. CLAUSE 2 IS NOT SATISFIED BY THIS ATTEMPT: the recorded macOS geometry-report timeout is neither reproduced nor explained here, and it stays open. The stale-pre-fix-binary story this attempt first argued is REFUTED by the campaign's own registry, inside the very gap that was cited as its authority. tui.client-input-backpressure (closed 2026-09-07 at 0bed7fe7) does cite compat/tui-pane-geometry.sh among its evidence and does record the cause exactly, crates/zz-tui/src/render.rs flush_output blocking the main event loop; but its resolution rules that stall out as the cause of a macOS geometry expiry, verbatim: "It also exited 0 at origin/main 012b4dcc before the fix, so the macbook expiry the cycle-17 gate recorded is not this stall reproducing there: that script drives the pane through the CLI's send-keys, not through the client's stdin, and its inner clients run inside an outer pinned tmux that reads their output continuously, so no backpressure ever builds. What remains on the macbook is unexplained and belongs to whoever next runs the tool there." Two refutations, either one sufficient. EMPIRICAL: 012b4dcc is 2026-09-07T10:45:51-03:00, after the fixture reached its current shape at 314c55e0 (00:15:42) and before the fix at 0bed7fe7 (13:31:08), which is exactly the window a stale binary would have to come from, and the registry records this fixture exiting 0 there - so a pre-fix binary running this fixture is measured as PASSING. MECHANISM, and it is platform-independent: the fixture's inner clients run inside an outer pinned tmux that drains their output continuously, so the backpressure flush_output stalled on never builds in this fixture at all; if no backpressure builds, the macOS pty write buffer's size is irrelevant and the pre-fix stall cannot fire on any platform, which the earlier draft's pty-buffer hedge does not reach. WHAT SURVIVES of that explanation is two measurements, neither of which reaches the macOS record: the fixture and the runtime are sound at this revision (six exit-0 runs, the measure() wait nowhere near its bound), and the named backpressure cause is measurably absent here (compat/run.sh --strict-geometry smoke/tui-client-input-backpressure exits 0 with 0 divergences). CLOSING CLAUSE 2 NEEDS a run of compat/tui-pane-geometry.sh on macOS with an attested binary, retaining the timeout dump this attempt added if the geometry-report wait fires. The timed-out binary's own revision is unrecoverable: the shared checkout's target/debug/zz was rebuilt on this box at 18:25 on 2026-09-09, so its hash says nothing about the record. FIXTURE CHANGE, in zone: a bounded wait that runs out now copies out, before the scratch tree is removed, which wait fired, both outer screens via capture-pane -p -e -S -, both servers' client and pane lists, the zz daemon's stdout and stderr, and each attached client's own stderr teed out of its pane; the fixture also pins ZZ_LOG_DIR into its scratch tree and scrubs XDG_STATE_HOME so it can no longer write into the box's real state directory. Proved by sabotage: file_has_two_fields was made to demand three fields, the fixture exited 2 with the record's own text "zz geometry report did not happen within 10 seconds" and left fourteen files, retained under timeout-diagnostics/; the edit was reverted and runs 4 to 6 are the unsabotaged fixture. That dump is what a macOS run would need to retain, and it is the part of this attempt clause 2 can still use. CLAUSE 3 RECORD, for TUI-004: at 120x24 the pin hands its pane 120 columns and zz hands its pane 91, rows 23 on both. The 29 column difference is the sidebar's 28 plus its 1 column border, the same arithmetic as AUTO_HIDE_COLUMNS = 80 + 28 + 1 = 109 in crates/zz-tui/src/sidebar.rs. Recorded, not asserted: tui.sidebar-auto-hide is a standing decision and TUI-004 owns changing it. FIXTURE LIMITATION AND A NEW DIVERGENCE: compat/status-row.sh exits 1 on this box, 2 of 11 comparisons, and the cause is the locale rather than the status row. Only the two steps that still carry the default status-right differ, and only in %b: the pin prints "09-set-26" and zz prints "09-Sep-26". The pin expands %b through libc strftime(3), which honours LC_TIME=pt_BR.UTF-8; zz expands it in crates/zz-mux/src/formats.rs:4707 format_datetime through chrono StrftimeItems and format_with_items, which is locale-independent and always English. Control run settles it: LC_ALL=C LC_TIME=C, same fixture, same binaries, exit 0, all 11 identical. The fixture is untouched by this branch, so it is red at origin/main on this box too and the red is not this lane's. No gap in compat/tmux-gaps.json records it, so it needs a registry owner; the fix would land in crates/zz-mux, which this cycle's wire rule puts out of reach, so it is measured and left. It is also a limitation of status-row.sh as a baseline: the fixture pins the pane title but not LC_TIME, so its default-row comparison carries the caller's locale; pinning the locale would hide the divergence rather than record it. OTHER PROOFS AT THIS TIP: compat/attached-client.sh exits 0, "attached-client compatibility: PASS". GATE, cycle 1, 2026-09-09 at 5dd932abb93c2e88f3190be42afeeed00ece6368 in /home/demfabris/dev/zz-gate-fixtures: every proof command above re-run at the merged tip on a zz this gate built itself, sha256 ddc5ae0f7be9e52b55dac82a8285c50f74a9684236986d277f54e1d8aa3b3254. Three geometry runs exit 0 at 4.8s, 4.5s and 4.7s, output byte-identical to all six committed runs; attached-client PASS; the backpressure scenario exit 0; tracker_test, both tracker checks and compat/check.sh exit 0. status-row.sh exits 1 exactly as recorded, %b only, and exits 0 under the LC_ALL=C control; the branch touches neither that fixture nor any crate source, so that red is origin/main's on this box and it is retained here as clause 3's fixture limitation. STATUS STAYS ACTIVE: clause 2 is open and cannot be closed on this box, because the recorded timeout happened on macOS and this box is Linux. The proof block recorded here stands for CLAUSES 1 AND 3 ONLY and is not a claim about clause 2. The reviewer's one confirmed defect was a nit addressed to the gate rather than to the branch - record the hash of the zz the gate builds, not environment.txt's 3cb6e284 - and it is done: ddc5ae0f7be9e52b55dac82a8285c50f74a9684236986d277f54e1d8aa3b3254 is a fourth distinct hash for source identical to origin/main, which settles that a debug build of zz is not reproducible here and that provenance rests on reproduction. SPLIT 2026-09-09: fabrico deferred the macOS reproduction (no macbook access now; the campaign continues on Linux) and the macOS half of clause 2 moved to TUI-013, added scope, so the baseline number never counts it as quietly done. What this obligation claims under the amended clause 2 is exactly what its proof block already records: the fixture retains the full timeout dump, proven by sabotage (fourteen files under timeout-diagnostics/), and the recorded macOS expiry is neither reproduced nor explained HERE - that work is TUI-013's, opening on this attempt's refutation of the stale-binary story and the retention machinery. decided 2026-09-09 by fabrico, relayed in-session to the orchestrator ('can we continue for now and record that test for later'); reversible - reopening TUI-001 and folding TUI-013 back undoes it.

items.title: Complete screen and interaction comparison
acceptance: Reuse existing attached-client drivers to compare all decoded cells, glyph widths, styles, cursor position/visibility/shape, geometry and resulting interaction state at named settled checkpoints.
Demonstrate that independent glyph, color/attribute, cursor and geometry changes fail with a useful location/state difference. Equivalent raw escape spellings must not fail.

Retain captures and environment at 80, 100, 109 and 120 columns, including small heights, split/zoom/resize and status off/on/multiple rows/top/bottom. Declare each controlled dynamic value and comparison rule.
items.evidence_note: MEASURED 2026-09-09 on alienware by the new fixture compat/tui-screen-diff.sh, which compares EVERY decoded cell of both screens plus the cursor at named settled checkpoints, both binaries attached inside one outer pinned tmux. zz sha256 3cb6e28437cd028b49c2c2eb07c4414a69226518bf2f287e7c52123d5bf70a38 at 576b6b74; pin d77c9dc6 sha256 df2cafcb212e8b69677dd57c2bd0c3bb59592eaf385d974ec0124526d6b63ee5. RESULT: 33 asserted checkpoints identical, 32 recorded, 65 recorded cursor differences; exit 0 twice in a row, and run 2's 195 capture files are byte-identical to run 1's. Asserted means every row of the outer pane matched byte for byte with its escapes and the asserted cursor tuple matched, at 80x24, 100x24 and 80x10, across fresh attach, status off, status on, split-window -v, resize-pane -Z, unzoom, an outer resize away and back, status 2, status-position top, and a row of CJK, combining and emoji glyphs. Not one cell differed. Two results beyond the count: the small height 80x10 behaves exactly like the wide sizes, and resizing the 120-column client down to 100 makes the two screens identical again cell for cell, so the sidebar is the whole of the 109-and-above difference and hiding it leaves nothing behind. CLAUSE 2, the demonstration: --self-check exits 0 only when four sabotages are each caught in their own channel and three equivalences are reported nowhere. glyph (one character of OUTPUT, from a file each side reads under its own HOME so the typed command is identical bytes) -> rows differ; colour (status-style bg=red on one side) -> rows differ; cursor (an unterminated line of a different length) -> the CURSOR tuple differs; geometry (split-window on one side) -> rows differ; and attribute order in a style, bg=red against bg=colour1, and \033[1mBOLD\033[0m against \033[01mBOLD\033[m -> nothing differs. Two of these were rebuilt after the first attempt measured something other than what it claimed. colour.c colour_fromstring gives red the value 1 and colour1 the value 1|COLOUR_FLAG_256, two DIFFERENT values, and yet both reach the outer grid as the same cell and capture-pane -e re-emits both as \e[41m, so the pair really does collapse: the fixture states the measurement, not the header-file reading. The first cursor sabotage sent a marker afterwards, which put the cursor back at a fresh prompt on both sides and reported no cursor difference at all; it now settles on a substring the two sides' own sabotage output share. CLAUSE 3, the covered subset: 80, 100, 109 and 120 columns, a small height at 80x10, split, zoom and resize, and status off, on, two rows, top and bottom are all driven, with all 195 captures and both cursor tuples retained. Every controlled dynamic value is declared in the fixture header with its rule: status-right '' (the clock, and the %d-%b-%y locale divergence TUI-001 recorded), status-left L, automatic-rename off plus rename-window win, select-pane -T (the recorded pane.runtime-facts decision), and an inner shell of ENV= PS1='$ ' exec /bin/sh handed to new-session and split-window. Global options are reset to each server's defaults before every attach so a case cannot leak into the next. WHAT REMAINS, and the one judgement the reviewer should make: all three clauses have evidence on this branch, so this is review, but ONE channel is compared and printed without being gated. Clause 1 asks for the cursor's SHAPE to be COMPARED and it is, on both sides at all 65 checkpoints, with both values printed every run; it is not asserted, because zz and the pin genuinely differ there today, and a sabotage of that channel could not be told apart from the standing divergence. A shape regression would therefore not turn this fixture red. If the reviewer reads clause 1 as requiring a gate rather than a comparison, downgrade this to active on that point alone; nothing else in the three clauses is short. THREE NEW DIVERGENCES, none with a registry owner, all recorded with both sides' bytes printed on every run. (a) CURSOR ATTRIBUTES, at 65 of 65 checkpoints: the pin reports shape=default blinking=0 colour=none and zz reports shape=block blinking=1 colour=#e5c07b, because crates/zz-tui/src/render.rs:1770-1799 writes DECSCUSR and an OSC 12 cursor colour on every cursor placement while the pin writes neither. Cursor position and visibility ARE asserted and match everywhere. (b) COLOUR CLASSES in the pane body: the same three cells written as named, indexed and RGB come back from the pin as \e[31m, \e[38;5;196m and \e[38;2;1;2;3m, and from zz as \e[38;2;205;0;0m, \e[38;2;255;0;0m and \e[38;2;1;2;3m. zz resolves the named and the indexed cell through its palette and hands the terminal RGB. tui.status-row's closed class-1 finding fixed the STATUS ROW; the pane body still promotes. (c) DEFAULT FOREGROUND: with status-style bg=colour4 and no foreground named, the pin emits no foreground and zz emits an explicit RGB 216,222,233. Under the default status-style the two agree byte for byte, which is why compat/status-row.sh never saw it. None of the three is fixable inside this cycle's zones: (a) is in crates/zz-tui/src outside TUI-001's excursion, and (b) and (c) reach the daemon's frame representation. Also not covered by this attempt: mouse, focus and bracketed paste (TUI-008), copy mode and search overlays (TUI-005), pane-border-status (TUI-004), more than one window, and a second attached client. THE SETTLE, measured not assumed: the marker alone was not enough. Two runs disagreed at the 80x24 zoom checkpoint, zz row 11 holding '$' in one and nothing in the next, because the shell writes the marker line and the prompt that follows it as two separate writes and a capture can land between them. A checkpoint is now settled when its marker is on the screen AND the screen has not changed between two polls; three consecutive runs after that fix were exit 0 with byte-identical captures. No wait in the fixture is a sleep. The timeout dump earned its place before it was sabotaged: the first full run timed out at 109x24 and the retained screen showed in one line that zz draws its sidebar to the LEFT of the pane there, so the marker shared its row with sidebar cells and a whole-line match could never succeed - a fixture fault, fixed by matching the marker as a substring. GATE, cycle 1, 2026-09-09 at 5dd932abb93c2e88f3190be42afeeed00ece6368: all three clauses re-proved at the merged tip on a zz this gate built itself, sha256 ddc5ae0f7be9e52b55dac82a8285c50f74a9684236986d277f54e1d8aa3b3254 - a THIRD independent binary after the worker's and the reviewer's. tui-screen-diff.sh exit 0 in 57.3s with the same summary line, and its 195 capture files plus its 29242-byte stdout are byte-identical to the committed evidence (diff -r exit 0, zero bytes); --self-check exit 0 in 24.1s with stdout byte-identical to the committed self-check.stdout.txt; attached-client PASS; both trackers and compat/check.sh exit 0. Nothing any fixture reported contradicts this obligation. STATUS STAYS REVIEW RATHER THAN VERIFIED, and the reason is the ledger's own rule, not a doubt about the evidence: compat/tui/tracker.py requires every dependency of a verified obligation to be verified too, and this obligation depends on TUI-001, which stays active on its open clause 2, so setting verified here would make tracker.py check fail. The proof block is recorded anyway: the cycle that closes TUI-001 clause 2 on macOS can flip this to verified on these measurements without re-running them. The reviewer confirmed no defect on this obligation. VERIFIED 2026-09-09: TUI-001 reached verified when its macOS clause split to TUI-013 (fabrico's deferral, recorded there), which satisfies the dependency rule; per this note's own provision the banked, thrice-reproduced measurements flip this obligation without re-running them. No new measurement was taken for this flip.
items.next_action: Done. The three recorded divergences still need registry owners (cursor attributes from crates/zz-tui/src/render.rs:1770-1799, named and indexed colours promoted to RGB in the pane body, and the explicit default foreground); the recorded half of the cursor tuple starts asserting the moment the first of those closes. items.title: Stock launcher, command and key behavior
acceptance: With clean config roots, compare bare packaged launch, attach and new-session on empty/live servers plus new-window and split-window. Assert stdout/stderr/exits, selected targets, pane kinds and the complete attached screen.
Drive unmodified stock split, chooser, rename, selection, zoom and detach bindings through actual stdin. Direct split-window creating a terminal does not substitute for testing its stock binding.

Test root bindings and application keys overlapping Ctrl-\ and Alt-s/Alt-S. Chrome cannot consume them outside its owning context. Exercise explicit config roots, -f and existing zz layering separately and record any policy conflict.
items.evidence_note: Measured on this box against pinned d77c9dc6 with two new differential fixtures, both driven inside one outer pinned tmux and both carrying a --self-check that sabotages every channel they compare. CLAUSE 1, compat/tui-launch-diff.sh, 29 comparisons at 80x24 (stdout+stderr+exit as one string, server facts, every decoded screen cell, the cursor tuple): attach-session on an empty server, attach-session -t <missing> on a live one, new-session -d twice, new-session -A -d, new-window -d, split-window -d and both against a missing target, all byte-identical to the pin; attach-session -t and a bare new-session both paint a screen identical to the pin's, cursor included. Two launcher behaviours are recorded, not asserted, because they are recorded decisions this obligation does not own: the bare launcher on a live server (zz runs new-session -A and attaches to `existing` where the pin makes a second session named `1`, semantic:bare-launcher-attach-current), and the bare launcher's screen (measured 2026-09-09 on Linux: `zz` with no arguments starts the native desktop client, which attaches to the daemon and leaves the terminal to its own output, while `tmux` with no arguments paints a session in the terminal it was run from; both leave exactly one attached session, which the case asserts). CLAUSE 1 FIX: the raw-terminal client wrote its log records onto the terminal it was about to paint. Two defects, both in crates/zz/src/diagnostics/mod.rs: process_role matched the literal argument `attach`, so `attach-session` and `new-session` (every spelling a user or a packaged client actually types) fell through to the `command` role and logged to stderr; and RingLogWriter mirrored every record to stderr whenever stderr was a terminal, so even the `tui` role wrote over the screen. Before the fix a `zz new-session -s fresh` left seven rows of `level=INFO role=tui ... process_start` on row 0 (launch-log-noise.before-fix.txt); after it the terminal carries zero log records on both sides, which is the launch-scrollback case. CLAUSE 2, compat/tui-stock-keys.sh, 50 cases at 80x24 and 100x24: every stock chord is typed into the ATTACHED CLIENT'S STDIN with send-keys against the OUTER pane, never executed as a command, and each case waits on a bounded observable, settles, then compares the whole screen, the cursor and a server-facts line. Measured before the fix: prefix % and prefix " ran the zz-native `split-picker` and opened a Picker pane where the pin opens a shell, and prefix s and prefix w ran `focus-sidebar` and moved focus into zz's own sidebar where the pin opens a session or window tree. acceptance: Ordinary tmux commands preserve the pinned canvas at narrow and wide dimensions; width never invokes the sidebar. Cover split, zoom, pane-border-status, small heights and resize restoration.
Compare full status/border presentation for default/custom formats, top/bottom/off/multiple rows, named/indexed/RGB colors, theme options and terminal light/dark reports.

items.evidence_note: CYCLE 4, CLAUSE 3: DRIVEN, MEASURED AND HALF FIXED. New fixture compat/tui-indicators.sh, 80x24, the outer-pinned-tmux driver copied from compat/status-row.sh and widened from one row to the whole screen plus the cursor tuple, at named settled checkpoints. 11 asserted comparisons identical and 5 recorded; --self-check plants three sabotages and one equivalence and catches all three. Evidence compat/tui/evidence/TUI-004/attempt-02/. TWO DIVERGENCES FOUND AND FIXED IN crates/zz-tui/src/render.rs, both zz chrome the pin does not draw. (1) THE ARMED PREFIX. OLD BEHAVIOUR: status_overlay painted ' PREFIX ' over the right of the status row whenever prefix_armed was set, so the two screens differed in eight cells for as long as a user held C-b. MEASURED PIN BEHAVIOUR: status.c redraws the row from the same formats it always uses and no default format reads #{client_prefix}, so the pin paints nothing at all; measured 2026-09-10 with both binaries attached in one outer pinned tmux and #{client_prefix} 1 on both clients. NEW STANCE: status_indicators splits in two - mode_indicators, the copy/view/search badges, is what the status ROW overlay carries, and status_indicators, those plus the hint, is what the SIDEBAR indicator row carries. The sidebar is client-local chrome with no counterpart in the pin that only focus-sidebar or a user binding shows, so the hint keeps a home and the shared row does not. PRODUCT DECISION: the status row a terminal client draws is the pin's row and carries no chrome of zz's own, so the armed-prefix hint lives on the sidebar's indicator line and nowhere else; a user who wants it at every width shows the sidebar. decided 2026-09-10 by the orchestrator under fabrico's TUI parity contract of 2026-09-09; reversible. prefix-armed and prefix-released are asserted whole. (2) THE CURSOR UNDER A MESSAGE. OLD BEHAVIOUR: with display-message up the raw TUI left the cursor visible at 79,23, where its last status-row write had put it. MEASURED PIN BEHAVIOUR: cursor_flag 0 at the PANE cursor's own position, 2,22 - server_client_reset_state (server-client.c:2073) drops MODE_CURSOR for a client whose status screen is being drawn and which has no prompt, and still calls tty_cursor, so the hidden cursor stays where the pane's cursor is. NEW STANCE: place_active_cursor places the pane cursor first and hides it after, under client_message_hides_the_cursor, whose guard mirrors status_overlay's - with the sidebar up and no command output the message is a sidebar row and the status row is untouched. A prompt keeps its cursor, so the check sits after the prompt branch. THREE FINDINGS RECORDED, NOT FIXED. (a) THE MESSAGE AND PROMPT STYLE, this fixture's own finding: the message row's and the prompt row's glyphs, columns and cursor are the pin's on both sides and the STYLE is not. The pin resolves message-style (bg=themeyellow,fg=themeblack, options-table.c:941) and message-command-style (options-table.c:910) and paints \\e[38;2;13;13;13m\\e[48;2;184;134;11m; the raw TUI paints its own overlay appearance, \\e[38;2;16;19;24m\\e[48;2;216;222;233m, and reads neither option. render.rs cannot fix it: the daemon publishes no resolved message style on StatusLine, so the client has nothing to dispatch on. THE FIELD IT WOULD NEED: StatusLine carries the resolved message-style and message-command-style, expanded in crates/zz-daemon/src/status.rs the way the row's own base_style already is, and status_overlay dispatches on them instead of overlay_style. That is a second protocol append and this lane's declared arm was the theme one, so it is left measured. The three cases run in text mode: every glyph, every column and the cursor asserted, the styles recorded. (b) COPY MODE, against the ACCEPTED gap options.native-mode-styles which holds option:copy-mode-position-format. window-copy.c:5228 draws copy-mode-position-format into the PANE grid at the top right and leaves the status row alone. Measured: the pin paints [0/45] at columns 74..79 of row 0 in copy-mode-position-style with its cursor in the pane at the copy cursor; the raw TUI paints nothing in the pane, a ' COPY 62/62 ' badge on the status row, and hides its cursor, and #{copy_position} and #{copy_position_limit} answer empty on zz where the pin answers 0 and 45. Recorded, never waived - the badge is printed both sides every run. copy-mode-restored is asserted. (c) THE VIEW SURFACE, measured before it was written rather than assumed. The pin has no view-mode COMMAND: window_view_mode (window-copy.c:184) is reached from cmd-run-shell.c:103 for the output of run-shell, from cfg.c:271 for a config error and from server-client.c:3061, and copy-mode -e is not a second surface at all - it is copy mode with scroll_exit set (window-copy.c:616) and both binaries answer #{pane_mode} copy-mode for it. So the case drives run-shell: the pin's pane goes to view-mode with the output as the whole screen and [0/0] at the top right, zz leaves #{pane_in_mode} at 0 and draws a client-side command-output overlay with a ' VIEW 1/21 ' badge. Same accepted gap. view-surface-restored is asserted. TWO MECHANICS THE FIXTURE HAD TO INVENT AND THE NEXT LANE SHOULD REUSE: it MARKS BEFORE IT ACTS, because a pane in copy mode, an armed prefix and an open command prompt each SWALLOW the send-keys marker tui-screen-diff.sh ends its checkpoints with, so every case types its marker first, settles on it, and only then applies the state; and the PREFIX IS A REAL KEYSTROKE into the outer pane, because send-keys writes into the PANE beneath the client's key table and can never arm a prefix. command-prompt -t <client> from a one-shot client does not return until the prompt is answered - measured by deadlocking a probe on it - so the prompt is opened the same way, prefix then colon. CLAUSES 1 AND 2 keep cycle 3's whole-screen evidence at 4cd23eb3 and its proof block; nothing about the sidebar decision, the canvas matrix or the cursor-attribute assertion is re-run or in doubt, and tui-screen-diff.sh, tui-pane-geometry.sh and status-row.sh all ran green again at this tip because the render.rs cursor change touches every checkpoint of the first of them. CYCLE 4, THE THEME ARM: LANDED WHOLE, ALL SIX HALVES IN ONE PUSH, AND THE THREE RECORDED ROWS ARE NOW ASSERTED. compat/status-row.sh reports all 14 comparisons identical with NONE recorded, where it reported 11 asserted and 3 recorded at cycle 3. record_step is deleted; the fixture has no recorded path left. THE CONSUMER HALF: the 21 names - `theme` plus ten dark-theme-* and ten light-theme-*, the roster server_client_update_theme_colours (server-client.c:1173) picks a half of per client - joined TMUX_OPTION_CONSUMERS, 118 to 139 at both hard-coded sites, scope counts [15,44,41,18] to [36,44,41,18]. That is what makes the names readable by name at all: parse_format_option gates every by-name option read on that roster, which is why #{E:dark-theme-green} and #{theme} answered empty before. compat_manifest_tests.rs enforces a partition between the roster and the option:<name> items in compat/tmux-gaps.json, so the same landing closes the 21 items of options.theme-palette, tracked 62 to 41; that gap was this lane's to close this cycle and it is closed with the measurement, along with tui.status-row, whose last item was presentation:tui-status-row-theme-colours-per-client. THE WIRE HALF: StatusLine gains `theme: ThemeColours`, ten TmuxColour values in colour_theme_table order, defaulting to the pin's dark set so a client that has not had a status line published keeps exactly what the raw TUI hard-coded; PROTOCOL_VERSION 99 to 100, a pure append, with the version claim and the frame-byte test updated. StatusLine::validate now rejects a theme slot that carries a theme colour, which is both the pin's rule (it skips a COLOUR_FLAG_THEME value and leaves the slot at 8) and what stops client-side resolution looping. TmuxColour and NOT an RGB triple, and that is the whole point: measured 2026-09-10 with both binaries attached in one outer pinned tmux, `set -s dark-theme-green colour124` leaves both sides as \\E[48;5;124m and not as truecolor. CYCLE 3'S SECOND REASON FOR NOT BUMPING IS RETIRED BY MEASUREMENT, not by nerve: crates/zz-client-ffi names no StatusLine and crates/zz-client-ffi/include/zz-client.h carries neither a protocol version nor a status layout, so the C ABI clients/ios and clients/macos consume does not change; clients/web references PROTOCOL_VERSION as a symbol and constructs no StatusLine, so it follows its own rebuild. THE DAEMON HALF: crates/zz-daemon/src/status.rs resolve_theme_colours, per client and per status line rather than on a client field, because that is where the daemon has the format tree the pin expands each option value through. `terminal` answers the fixed ANSI column [0,7,7,0,2,3,1,4,6,5] and reads no option, `light` and `dark` force their half, `detect` follows the scheme the client reported at hello (the daemon already keeps client_color_schemes) and falls back to dark the way THEME_UNKNOWN does. Each chosen value is expanded as a FORMAT before it is parsed, which is not decoration: every default in the roster is #{?#{e|>=:#{client_colours},256},<x11 name>,<basic name>}, so an unexpanded value parses as nothing. THE CLIENT HALF: crates/zz-tui/src/render.rs resolves every themeX in the composed status line through the published set - StyledLine::resolve_theme substitutes the slot's TmuxColour into the segment before write_ground ever sees it, so the class survives without threading a palette pair through twenty call sites. The status row and the sidebar's mirror of it only; every other TUI surface that can name a theme colour keeps zz's theme under the recorded presentation:tui-status-row-theme-defaults decision, whose scope is exactly that. THE PIECE NO CYCLE-3 PLAN NAMED, and it is why the arm looked dead after the resolver and the wire were both in: A REFRESH TRIGGER. A write to a theme option raised no effect, so the status was never re-rendered and a running client never saw the change. Measured by setting dark-theme-green BEFORE the client attached, which produced the pin's \\E[48;5;124m, and after, which produced nothing. crates/zz-mux/src/command.rs stored_scalar_execution now answers StatusFormatsChanged for the roster. WHAT IS PROVED AND WHERE: compat/status-row.sh at 79x24 under LC_ALL=C LC_TIME=C, all 14 identical; a zz-daemon unit test that walks the stock resolution, the indexed class, the light half, the terminal column and the colour-8 fallback for a value that names a theme colour; a zz-tui unit test that the wire default equals the table the client used to hard code and that a published slot's class reaches the escape. STATUS: all three acceptance clauses have evidence at this tip. Clause 3's indicator half is the new fixture and its two render fixes, and its theme sentence is the landing above. The playbook says a waived comparison or a skipped case is recorded, never counted, and the divergence those two cases record is the ACCEPTED gap options.native-mode-styles (option:copy-mode-position-format), so counting them would count an accepted gap as progress, which the campaign forbids. Whether that falls under clause 2's "full status presentation" is for triage; it is recorded, not counted, either way, and it is raised as a cycle-4 residual. acceptance: Compare stock emacs and vi pane copy tables, forward/backward search editing, repeat search, numeric counts, line/page movement, selection, rectangles, copy and cancel through actual input.

items.evidence_note: Measured 2026-09-10 (cycle 5, copy lane, attempt-02 and the fix pass after its adversarial review) at 80x24 against pin d77c9dc6 with compat/tui-copy-mode.sh, which types the stock chords into both attached clients inside one outer pinned tmux and compares the decoded rows, the same rows without styles, the outer cursor tuple, the logical copy position, the view, the paste buffer byte for byte, and the three copy-mode formats inside and outside the mode. At the fix pass: 115 cases, all 115 assert at least one channel, every asserted channel identical on three runs; --self-check meets 21 of 21 expectations. STATUS active, not review: 12 current-match cases and the emacs search backspace are recorded SIBLING:modes under MATCH_REASON, which the batch did not assign to the modes lane, and the modes branch at 5a85f44e does not paint copy-mode-match-style or copy-mode-current-match-style (the review's reading), so clauses 1, 2 and 3 stay open until the orchestrator names that owner. CLOSED IN THIS ATTEMPT, each asserted and each with its own sabotage. (1) Half page and search landing: window_copy_pageup1 and window_copy_pagedown1 move the VIEW by screen_size_y/2 and keep the cursor's screen row, and a search lands through window_copy_scroll_to (a cursor off screen goes a quarter screen above the bottom, or to the top when its line is in the first screen). zz used to move the cursor row and leave the view: after the forward search both now find line-12 needle-12 at row 12 / scroll 39, where zz used to sit at row 0 / scroll 27. crates/zz-terminal session.rs page_copy_cursor and scroll_copy_view_to_cursor. The half-page cases and the five search cases per table after the prompt now assert the view; the sabotage (a half page on one side, twelve counted cursor-ups on the other) lands in the view channel alone with the logical line identical. (2) Whole page: the pin steps screen_size_y-2 = 22 lines and keeps the cursor row; zz stepped 24 and moved the cursor row. From line-60 at row 21 / scroll 0 both now land on line-38 at row 21 / scroll 22 after page-up and back on line-60 at row 21 / scroll 0 after page-down, so both page cases per table assert every channel (they asserted nothing in cycle 4). Sabotage: a page on one side, twenty-four counted cursor-ups on the other, caught in facts. (3) The vi rectangle past the end of the last selected line keeps its final newline: window_copy_get_selection only removes it when mode-keys is emacs or lastex <= ey_last. zz now copies the same 36 bytes as the pin (`line-58 filler-58\nline-59 filler-59\n`) where it copied 35. The rule is the pin's for an ordinary vi selection too (a selection ending on an empty line keeps the newline), unit-tested in mode_revision.rs format_selection. Sabotage: the same rectangle with the pin's mode-keys switched to emacs just before the copy, caught in buffer (35 against 36). (4) Prefix precedence inside a copy table: server-client.c:1417 makes the prefix win over copy-mode's C-b (cursor-left) and copy-mode-vi's C-b (page-up). crates/zz-protocol key.rs KeyEngine now arms the prefix from a mode table and returns to that table once the prefix binding ran, was unbound, timed out or was cancelled (cancel_prefix, which crates/zz-daemon's cancel_prefix now calls instead of dropping the table). $table-prefix-takes-precedence asserts every channel, so the copy position and the view, which the copy binding would move, are now channels the keypress can fail; the reviewer's cycle-4 nit (a buffer-only assertion at a checkpoint with two empty buffers) is closed. $table-prefix-returns-to-the-copy-table types `[` (copy-mode, which the pin ignores for a pane already in the mode) and a cursor-up, and asserts the copy table answers again. Sabotage: C-b as page-up on one side and as the prefix on the other, caught in facts. (5) selection_active and rectangle_toggle answered empty on zz inside copy mode. CopyModeFacts now carries the session's rectangle flag and a live selection still being extended (data->cursordrag); crates/zz-daemon status.rs answers them and both moved to the delegated copy-mode partition. assert_mode_formats compares them with pane_search_string through display-message -p at settled checkpoints inside and outside the mode: 1/0 after a selection, 1/1 with the rectangle on, 0/0 after the searches, empty outside the mode, identical on both. Sabotage: a search, the rectangle toggle and a selection on one side only, caught in the formats check. (6) Found and fixed on the way: after Enter in the emacs incremental search the raw TUI left the prompt row on screen, because a closing prompt only asked for a partial repaint and the search had already moved the view, so no pane row was dirty. crates/zz-tui app.rs now repaints the whole screen when the prompt closes. emacs-ordinary-pane-search-submit asserts text since; copy-mode-before-the-prompt-repaint-fix.txt is a corpus run of the previous fixture revision against the binary without that fix, which shows the stale `(search down) needle` row. Sabotage: a search prompt open on one side only, caught in text. (7) THE SEARCH OUTLIVES THE MODE, the review's blocker. The pin keeps the last search on the pane: window_copy_search writes wp->searchstr (window-copy.c:4508), format_cb_pane_search_string answers from it inside and outside a mode (format.c:2418), and window_copy_common_init copies it into the next mode with searchtype up (window-copy.c:566). The review measured zz at b050b375 on a vi pane of 80 lines with PROBELATE on line 70: `/PROBELATE` Enter, q, C-b [, n left zz at cursor 2,23, row 23, line [$] where the pin landed on 0,11, row 11, line [PROBELATE], and #{pane_search_string} answered empty on zz against PROBELATE on the pin after q and on the re-entry; the emacs table the same with needle. crates/zz-terminal session.rs now keeps the pane's last copy-mode search on the terminal actor (run_terminal's pane_search, written where run_copy_mode_search sets the mode's search, with the regex flag demoted the way the pin demotes it), publishes it as TerminalSession::pane_search_string, seeds a fresh entry's search from it with the direction backward, and latches data->searchall so an entry's first search recounts its matches; crates/zz-daemon status.rs answers pane_search_string from the pane's terminal, so it answers after q and on a fresh entry too. Sabotages: a search on one side only, then q and a re-entry on both, caught in the formats check after q and again on the re-entry; n on a fresh entry on the pin side only, caught in cursor and facts; n on one side and N on the other on a fresh entry after a forward search, caught in facts. Unit tests: zz-terminal the_pane_keeps_its_last_search_and_a_fresh_entry_searches_up_for_it (the pane record after cancel, the up direction, the recount) and zz-daemon pane_search_string_outlives_the_copy_session_and_seeds_the_next_entry (the format through display-message after cancel and on the re-entry, and search-again there). STILL RECORDED, ALL SIBLING:modes, 31 cases; every glyph, the cursor, the logical position, the view and the buffer assert through all of them. ASSIGNED to the modes lane by the batch: the selection style (12 cases: begin-selection, selection-extends, rectangle-on, rectangle-off, rectangle-inside-line, rectangle-past-end-of-line per table; the pin paints copy-mode-selection-style, zz a reverse-video overlay one cell further), the command prompt palette (5 cases: search prompt and typed per table, and the vi backspace), and the position indicator (presentation-copy-mode-position: the pin draws [0/40] into the pane's top row from copy-mode-position-format, zz paints a COPY badge on the status row). NOT ASSIGNED by the batch, owner for the orchestrator to name: the current-match style (12 cases: search submit, again, reverse, backward, re-entry search-again and forward-search re-entry searches-up per table; the pin paints copy-mode-current-match-style bg #cd00cd, zz reverse video) and the emacs search backspace, whose reason carries the prompt palette and the current match together. That painting lives in crates/zz-tui render.rs, the modes lane's zone this cycle, so this lane cannot land it. Under fabrico's TUI parity contract these are the TUI portion of options.native-mode-styles and presentation.native-status; the old behaviour was a reverse-video overlay, a native palette prompt and a status-row badge, the pin's measured behaviour is the one above; decided 2026-09-10 by the orchestrator under fabrico's TUI parity contract of 2026-09-09; reversible. CLAUSE 3 INVENTORY, covered subset rather than complete table coverage. Typed in BOTH tables: entry (prefix [), cursor-up, cursor-down, start-of-line, end-of-line, halfpage-up, halfpage-down, page-up, page-down, the numeric prefix (M-5 in emacs, 5 in vi), begin-selection, rectangle-toggle on and off, copy-pipe-and-cancel on an ordinary selection, two rectangle copies with the rectangle still on (right edge inside every selected line, and past the end of the last), cursor-right under a numeric prefix, cancel, the forward and backward search prompts with editing (search-forward-incremental / search-backward-incremental in emacs, search-forward / search-backward in vi), search-again, search-reverse, the C-b prefix collision and the return to the copy table after it, a live mode-keys change picked up by the next entry, a live bind-key -T copy-mode-vi picked up without a re-entry, and the return to terminal input after cancel. NOT typed here and resting on copy-mode.action-fidelity's send-keys -X closure, which is the command path: the jump family (f F t T ; ,), word and space motions (w b e W B E), paragraphs, matching brackets, marks (X, M-x), history-top and history-bottom, top/middle/bottom line, the scroll family (C-y C-e J K C-Up C-Down z), other-end, select-line, select-word, append-selection-and-cancel, copy-pipe-end-of-line-and-cancel, back-to-indentation, goto-line, refresh-toggle, toggle-position, recentre-top-bottom, cursor-centre-horizontal, previous-prompt, next-prompt, and every mouse binding (keys.copy-mode-native-mouse, accepted). Ordinary-pane search stays separate from command-output search: the stock chords take command-prompt -T search on both binaries, and zz's own copy-mode-search-prompt command (no pin counterpart) still answers `terminal search is unsupported here` on an ordinary pane, measured and printed by the native-search-command group on every run. A SETTLE RACE IN THIS FIXTURE, FOUND AND FIXED: the two rectangle checkpoints settled on two identical polls with no observable, and each emacs M-5 C-f pair goes through the numeric prompt, so under load zz's screen could hold still between two prompt round trips and the comparison ran before the last counted cursor-right landed: zz's copy cursor at column 15 in one early run and at column 5 in a loaded run at 3ced0ea6 (copy-mode-settle-race-before-the-fix.txt), against the pin's 20 both times. be67a0d5 makes both checkpoints wait for #{copy_cursor_x} to reach the typed column on both sides, so a side that never reaches it is still an asserted difference; the three corpus runs and the self-check at be67a0d5 ran concurrently under the same load and are green. acceptance: Declare a finite capability matrix covering legacy/extended keys, user keys, paste, focus/mouse, color/theme replies, Unicode widths and alternate-screen restoration.
Compare effects and client facts for cells/styles and global flags including -2, -u and -T. Ignored flags and waived capability cases remain visible obligations.

items.evidence_note: Measured on alienware against pinned tmux d77c9dc6 with both binaries attached inside one outer pinned tmux; evidence at compat/tui/evidence/TUI-009/attempt-01. The new fixture compat/tui-caps.sh declares the finite capability matrix in its header and drives 63 asserted rows and 41 recorded rows over three green runs with identical row dispositions, plus five sabotages and a control. THE DECODER DOES THE WORK: the outer pinned tmux decodes each inner client's mode-setting sequences into its own pane state and publishes them as formats, so alternate screen, bracketed paste, cursor visibility and shape, autowrap, origin mode, synchronized output, application keypad, the five mouse modes and #{pane_key_mode} are compared as decoded modes rather than as bytes, and capture-pane -p -e is the colour-class channel. ASSERTED AND IDENTICAL: alternate screen armed on attach, bracketed paste, cursor visibility and shape, origin mode, synchronized output, mouse_any/sgr/standard/utf8, pane_key_mode VT10x under extended-keys off, client_termname, client_utf8 and client_flags with no flag, the entire 16-row mode tuple after detach (alternate-screen restoration, which is the acceptance clause's own channel), the five flag-diagnostic rows, and two channels the matrix expected only to name. UNICODE WIDTHS TURNED OUT ASSERTABLE: options.terminal-engine-limits is accepted on the grounds that zz keeps its engine's own widths and takes no override, which says nothing about whether they agree with the pin's; with UTF-8 clients on both sides a wide CJK pair, a base letter with a combining acute and an astral emoji leave the outer cursor at the same column (20,0) and produce the identical decoded line, asserted in widths/cursor and widths/line, and a sixth sabotage adds one wide codepoint to the pin's sample alone to prove the case can fail. THE UTF-8 LOCALE TOO: attached under LANG=C.UTF-8 and LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 with no flag, BOTH sides come up client_utf8 1 with UTF-8 in client_flags, so zz already implements the pin's locale fallback exactly and what it lacks is only the flag that overrides it. CLAUSE 2, THE THREE FLAGS. Parsing and diagnostics are pin-exact on both binaries modulo the program name: -2 -V, -u -V and -T sixel -V exit 0, a bare -T exits 1 with 'option requires an argument -- T' and the pin's usage block, an unknown option exits 1 with 'unknown option -- W' and the same block. Applying them is where zz stops. On TERM=xterm with LANG=C and LC_ALL=C (the locale matters: this box's LANG would set CLIENT_UTF8 through the pin's own fallback and hide the flag), -u takes the pin's client_utf8 from 0 to 1 and adds UTF-8 to client_flags while zz changes nothing; -T sixel adds sixel to the pin's client_termfeatures while zz changes nothing; -2 adds 256, which the pin's client already has, so its own-side delta is empty and matches zz's empty delta - that row is recorded, not claimed as parity. crates/zz/src/lib.rs drops all three at "'2' | 'q' | 'u' | 'v' => {}" and at the 'T' arm, which reads its argument and discards it; -q and -v are correct there, because -q is a no-op in the pin too and -v is its log level. THREE IGNORED FLAGS ARE VISIBLE OBLIGATIONS, NOT PASSES, and each names what it needs: -u needs the attach to carry the client's UTF-8 flag, which crates/zz-daemon/src/daemon.rs client_uses_utf8 would read before falling back to the environment it reads today (TMUX set, else LC_ALL/LC_CTYPE/LANG containing utf-8, the pin's fallback without the flag that overrides it); -2 and -T need the attach to carry a feature list that client_term_features merges, where it derives the whole roster from TERM and COLORTERM. Both are crates/zz-protocol plus crates/zz-daemon, outside this obligation's zones, and the first is a wire change. EXTENDED KEYS, a finding: under extended-keys on the pin arms Eneks (\e[>4;2m) and the decoder records Ext 2, while zz arms NOTHING and the decoder records VT10x. CORRECTED AT THE GATE 2026-09-10: this first read "zz arms the Kitty protocol (\e[>3u) and the pin's CSI table ignores it", which is not the mechanism behind the measurement. tty.rs writes \e[>3u only when guard.kitty_keyboard is set and supports_kitty_keyboard reads TERM/TERM_PROGRAM for ghostty, kitty, wezterm, foot or zz; the fixture attaches with TERM=xterm-256color, which matches none, so no extended-key request is sent at all. Measured by capturing the attach stream against a throwaway daemon at this tip: 0 occurrences of \e[>3u under TERM=xterm-256color, 1 under TERM=xterm-ghostty, with \e[?1004h present under both. The pin's single { 'u', "", INPUT_CSI_RCP } entry remains a true source read but describes a kitty-class TERM this fixture does not drive. Attached to a tmux-class outer terminal zz gets no extended keys at all; meeting the pin means arming modifyOtherKeys and decoding the \e[27;<mod>;<key>~ form, which crates/zz-tui/src/terminal_event.rs does not do (it decodes only the Kitty \e[<key>;<mod>u form) and which is not in this obligation's zone list. Two things narrow that finding: under DEFAULT options both binaries have extended-keys off, the pin arms nothing and the fixture's legacy case asserts pane_key_mode VT10x on both, so the gap opens only for a user who turns the option on; and set -s extended-keys on visibly changes nothing on zz, which CONFIRMS the accepted stance on options.client-terminal-negotiation (the option is store-only and the raw TUI arms its own fixed sequence set) rather than contradicting it. What this adds to that stance, and what the gap does not record, is the consequence: on a tmux-class outer terminal zz's \e[>3u is a no-op, so the raw TUI has no extended-key channel there at all. CLAUSE 3, MEASURED FIRST. The class is lost in the terminal engine, not in the TUI: crates/zz-terminal/src/model.rs PackedStyle stores foreground: u32 and background: u32, a packed 24-bit RGB with no palette index, and its doc comment says 'resolved'; ATTR_EXPLICIT_RGB keeps the explicit/named bit but not which index was named. The wire (terminal_codec.rs push_u32(style.foreground_raw())) and the renderer (render.rs "\x1b[38;2;{};{};{}m") are faithful to a value that was already classless, and the same renderer proves it is not the problem: chrome travels as TmuxColour with Basic, Indexed and Rgb arms and write_ground spells each one back in its own class. Measured: SGR 31 reaches the outer grid as \e[31m on the pin and \e[38;2;205;0;0m on zz; SGR 38;5;42 as \e[38;5;42m against \e[38;2;0;215;135m, which is exactly what the 6x6x6 cube says index 42 is; explicit RGB is identical on both and asserts. A fix needs the source class per ground in PackedStyle plus a wire field, which is not this cycle's. WHAT CLAUSE 3 EARNED ANYWAY: once an OSC 4 entry exists for colour 1 the pin stops emitting the index and resolves the cell through the pane palette, so both sides put the identical RGB on the outer terminal for the foreground AND the background that entry paints; the fixture asserts colours/palette named cell, named background and rgb cell, and records the untouched indexed cell beside them so the case cannot pass by accident. RECORDED EMISSION DIFFERENCES, none of which moves a cell (tui-screen-diff.sh is green at this tip, 111 asserted checkpoints identical): wrap_flag 1 against 0, because tty.rs writes \e[?7l on entry and \e[?7h on exit and a renderer that positions every cell explicitly needs autowrap off to write the last cell of the last row; mouse_all_flag 0 against 1 and mouse_button_flag 1 against 0, because zz arms \e[?1003h for the whole attach where the pin arms \e[?1002h and raises MODE_MOUSE_ALL only while a menu is up - zz's TUI does consume motion (input.rs maps Moved to Motion), so it is a scope difference and narrowing it is app.rs; keypad_flag and keypad_cursor_flag 1 against 0, because the pin sends smkx and zz sends neither, which is confined since the outer terminal then sends normal-mode CSI arrows and that is what terminal_event.rs parse_csi decodes. NAMED, NOT DRIVEN, and not silently absent: focus reporting, because the pin publishes no pane format for focus mode so this decoder cannot see it - read from source it is NOT equal, tty.c arms Enfcs only when focus-events is on and its default is 0 while tty.rs writes \e[?1004h on every attach; user keys and Unicode widths, which belong to accepted gaps; and the individual OSC 10/11 and DA replies, whose effect the negotiation row measures as a whole. A MEASUREMENT THAT ADDS TO A GAP THIS LANE DOES NOT OWN: options.client-terminal-negotiation records that zz opens no terminfo database; 06-pin-feature-negotiation.txt adds that the PIN does not read its client feature list from the terminfo entry either - attached to the same outer pinned tmux under vt100, xterm, xterm-256color and screen-256color it answers the identical list every time, including 256 and RGB on vt100 whose entry has neither, because tty-keys.c adds features straight from the DA parameters. That does not contradict the recorded decision, so the gap is left alone; it is why -2's 256 is redundant on any terminal that answers and why client_colours reads 16777216 against zz's 16 on TERM=xterm. No Rust source changed on this branch. THE SECOND RECORDED PANE-BODY DIVERGENCE, added at the gate 2026-09-10 because the batch named two and the lane measured one: compat/tui-screen-diff.sh's `default-fg` checkpoint records that zz writes an explicit RGB foreground where the pin leaves the foreground default. Measured at the accumulated cycle-4 tip under status-style bg=colour4: the pin emits \e[44m and zz emits \e[38;2;216;222;233m\e[44m, glyphs, columns and cursor identical. The emission point IS inside this lane's zone - crates/zz-tui/src/render.rs write_ground takes the None arm when a style names no colour and calls write_rgb_ground with default_foreground, while a style that names `default` or `terminal` already takes the \e[39m arm - but emitting \e[39m there is NOT a safe one-line change: \e[39m is the outer terminal's default foreground and the fallback is zz's theme foreground, and the raw TUI paints its own ground under that glyph, so the swap can put a terminal-default foreground on a zz-painted background. Meeting the pin needs a decision about what a zz client's default foreground means when the client paints its own background, which belongs beside presentation:tui-status-row-theme-defaults. Traced in full in compat/tui/evidence/TUI-009/attempt-01/11-default-foreground-trace.txt, measured and NOT fixed, and raised as a cycle-4 residual because no accepted decision covers it. GATE 2026-09-10, CYCLE 4, alienware, final pre-records tip 2b406cc15381208b0b51a80096f1af691521a299: STAYS AT REVIEW. The reviewer approved with fixes and both must-fixes are applied at the gate: the extended-key mechanism corrected above (under the fixture's TERM zz sends no extended-key request at all, reproduced at the gate by capturing the attach stream, 0 occurrences of \e[>3u under xterm-256color against 1 under xterm-ghostty), and the second pane-body divergence the batch named, now measured and traced in 11-default-foreground-trace.txt. Under the stock palette zz promotes a named cell (SGR 31) and an indexed cell (38;5;42) to truecolor where the pin keeps the class, because PackedStyle carries no class to keep. The default-foreground divergence is recorded beside it. Reviewer nit (d) stands: delta-client_flags and delta-client_termfeatures sit in the global FACT_RECORDED, so the -2 and -T own-side delta channels never assert anywhere.

items.title: Slow output, recovery and client lifecycle
acceptance: Measure prolonged terminal backpressure past the writer budget, deliver an observable bound key while undrained, and verify bounded memory and response within a declared reference-derived deadline.
Resume reading and compare the final screen. Detach under backlog and prove no queued paint appears after terminal restoration.
Exercise different-sized simultaneous terminal clients, read-only attach, detach/reattach and supported transport recovery. Compare selected targets, geometry, focus and final screen.
items.evidence_note: All three clauses measured and proved on this box (alienware, CachyOS, 16 cores) on 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-10. CLAUSE 1, MEASURED FIRST with compat/tui-output-backpressure.sh, whose relay (compat/tui-output-relay.py) is a pty in an outer pinned tmux pane that stops reading on command while keys keep flowing, at 80x24 with the registry's 45 s undrained window and a bound F5. BEFORE, at origin/main bfd05821: pinned tmux d77c9dc6 answered in 0.033 s and grew 0 kB over the window from a 4892 kB baseline; zz did not answer within the 12 s the registry recorded and grew 6144 kB from a 105956 kB baseline. AFTER: zz answers in 0.025 s and grows 6572 kB. Memory was bounded on both sides before and after, so the 4 MiB budget was never what cost the client its liveness and the budget did not move; what changed is the behaviour past it. crates/zz-tui/src/writer.rs now drops the whole queue the way tty.c tty_block_maybe drains its out buffer, keeps dropping for the pin's 100 ms TTY_BLOCK_INTERVAL, and clears the block on the first interval that dropped less than BLOCK_STOP, keeping the pin's 64:1 START:STOP ratio against a whole-paint queue. Clearing it repaints from the model the way tty_timer_callback sets CLIENT_ALLREDRAWFLAGS and calls tty_invalidate: render.rs throws away its painted state on a drop and app.rs takes a MainEvent::Repaint from the writer's block timer. Control bytes a dropped paint carried go back to the front of the next paint, because a mode change is not something a repaint reproduces. The declared response deadline is 1.000 s, twenty times the 0.050 s the registry recorded for the pin, and the pin runs as a side of the fixture so every run proves the deadline is achievable here. CLAUSE 2: after the relay resumes, the recovered screen is identical to the pin cell for cell above the status row with the same cursor tuple, and after a detach taken while undrained zz wrote 40 bytes and ZERO escape bytes after leaving the alternate screen. CLAUSE 3, in compat/attached-client.sh (--lifecycle runs the three new probes alone): different-sized simultaneous clients at 90x20 and 70x30 under every window-size rule, which corrected the premise that the pin sizes to the smallest - options-table.c defaults window-size to WINDOW_SIZE_LATEST, so the untouched default follows the most recently used client (70x30 then 90x20 as each is used) and only an explicit smallest takes the componentwise 70x20, largest the componentwise 90x30, with both clients keeping their own geometry throughout; read-only attach proved in all four of the pin's parts, typing that never reaches the pane, a bound run-shell that never runs, a bound switch-client that does, and a live screen, with the refusals proved in order against a bound key pressed by the read-write client rather than by a sleep; and three detach/reattach cycles alternating a client-key detach with a server-side detach-client against the tty, each one asserting the selected target, the client geometry, the focus flag and the marker still on the screen. Supported transport recovery measured beyond that: with the real daemon killed (the zz daemon forks, so the pid that owns the socket is the child), both binaries print [server exited unexpectedly] and exit 1, the pin within 0.05 s and zz within 0.1 s. Every added case sabotaged once and caught in its own assertion, and the whole fixture goes red against a build from before the drop path. RECORDED, not asserted: the cursor shape/blink/colour divergence (canvas lane owns it); the status row's explicit default foreground, byte for byte the same before this change and after it; and that the pin's client never leaves an alternate screen at all, so its escape tail has no restoration point to be after. tui.client-output-queue-budget is closed on this proof. GATE 2026-09-10: the review's second nit is recorded rather than fixed, because fixing it is a behaviour change that would need this fixture re-proved against a new timing claim, which is a lane's work. Measured and confirmed at the gate: tmux tty.c tty_block_maybe zeroes tty->discarded when it starts a block (tty.c:241), so the pin's first 100 ms interval counts only bytes offered after the drop and its block can end after one interval, while crates/zz-tui/src/writer.rs submit sets discarded = queued + bytes.len(), folding the whole dropped queue into the first interval; BLOCK_STOP is QUEUE_BUDGET/64, so the first tick always continues and a zz block lasts at least two intervals. The 64:1 START:STOP ratio claim is exact; the block START rule is not the pin's, and this sentence exists so a later reader does not take it for the pin's. Bounded, and input stays live throughout. The lane also rewrote its own record's sources array, which is a field a worker may not write; the gate kept the corrected array because the reviewer verified it against the diff and it is factually right.
items.next_action: Closed, and with it the last blocker TUI-012 had besides TUI-008 and TUI-009. The gap tui.client-output-queue-budget is closed in compat/tmux-gaps.json with its before and after numbers. Routed, not closed: the status-row divergence this fixture records is a NEW occurrence of the known explicit-default-foreground difference under the DEFAULT status-style rather than the non-default one tui.status-row names, it appears only on a full repaint, and compat/tui-screen-diff.sh is green and does not see it - whoever picks up tui.status-row should widen its wording. The server-death half of transport recovery stays recorded, not asserted: it came from an ad-hoc probe that is not on the branch and no fixture guards those 0.05 s / 0.1 s numbers.
